preamble: Retroflexion of the alveolar tap [ɾ] to the retroflex flap [ɽ], with the tongue tip curled back so that it strikes the postalveolar region. It occurs as an allophone of the tap phoneme. Some European Portuguese speakers, including in word-final position (falar [fɐˈläɽ]), and some caipira and sertanejo speakers in Brazil use [ɽ] for /ɾ/. In Havana, a retroflex variety of Cuban Spanish has [ɽʂ] for coda /ɾ/ before /s/ (marzo ma[ɽʂ]o), where the variety without retroflexion has [ss] or [d˺s] (Arias 2019).

languageExamples.language: Portuguese (some European, caipira and sertanejo speakers)
languageExamples.context: Speaker-dependent realization of /ɾ/; attested word-finally (falar), between vowels (madeira) and in the coda (gargalhar)

examples.note: Arias (2019): the first element "se mantiene como líquido", unlike fue[d˺s]a, where it becomes a non-liquid.
